hook.headline: Your filament settings already work. Move them without rebuilding them.
altHeadlines: What if moving slicers did not mean starting over?
A migration tool that refuses to guess

features.heading: See the exact plan before anything changes
features.rationale: The product centers operator review and deterministic planning before writes.

features.heading: Know what was created and what is still pending
benefitLines: Local creation stays separate from cloud state
Bambu loading and cloud IDs are recorded independently
features.rationale: The evidence ledger prevents local, cloud, and AMS states from being collapsed into one claim.

features.heading: Restore only what the run still owns
features.rationale: Path-owned journals and hash checks keep restore bounded and preserve later external changes.

positioning.differentiator: A local-first Windows migration workstation that resolves inherited filament settings, freezes exact local outputs for review, and records evidence without claiming cloud or AMS states it cannot prove.

audience.who: Windows users who already trust filament presets in OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio and want those settings available for official Bambu printers without rebuilding each profile by hand.
painPoints: Re-entering known filament settings is slow and easy to get wrong.
Profile inheritance makes the effective values hard to inspect manually.
A local file, a cloud ID, and AMS visibility are different states but are often treated as one.
Broad restore operations can overwrite files changed after migration.

use: restore only what the run owns

objections.objection: Will this edit my source profiles while it scans them?
objections.response: Discovery and planning are read-only. Source files are resolved for review and are not modified.

objections.objection: Does local creation prove the profile is in Bambu cloud or visible in AMS?
objections.response: No. Local creation, Bambu Studio loading, cloud ID assignment, and human AMS verification are recorded as separate evidence levels.

objections.objection: Can restore overwrite work changed after the migration?
objections.response: A changed file is excluded from restore rather than overwritten.

switchingForces.push: Rebuilding profiles by hand repeats work and can lose settings hidden through inheritance.
switchingForces.pull: A reviewed local plan can preserve trusted settings and generate the exact selected outputs.
switchingForces.habit: Manual recreation is familiar and feels controllable even when it is repetitive.
switchingForces.anxiety: Users do not want a migration tool to overwrite profiles, invent cloud evidence, or touch unrelated account files.

proofPoints.claim: A frozen plan records source fingerprints and exact destination byte state.
Restore preserves files changed externally after commit.
Spool Ledger requests, stores, and transmits no Bambu credentials.
Copied-root acceptance reproduces 16 slicing presets, 64 custom profiles, and 64 sidecars in a temporary account copy while protected live-root hashes remain unchanged.
The approved live demonstration proves local creation, Bambu Studio loading, and unique cloud IDs for two Overture profiles; AMS verification remains pending.

cta: Review the workflow and download Spool Ledger

narration.text: Your filament settings already work. Moving slicers should not mean rebuilding them.
Choose the profiles and official printers you want. Spool Ledger resolves the settings and shows the exact local plan before anything changes.
Review every output, conflict, and missing dependency before commit.
After the run, local creation, Bambu loading, cloud IDs, and AMS checks stay separate.
If you restore later, files changed by another process are preserved.
Review the workflow and download Spool Ledger.
